advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the entrypoint comment with the actual _reads.py guard (dir-existence, not convergence), or strengthen the guard to detect an unconverged store.
evidence: Dockerfile comment: "# store_uninitialized until the store is converged, rather than reporting [] and"
src/rebar/_reads.py:42: `if not os.path.isdir(tracker):` — guard fires only on ABSENT dir, not on an unconverged/partial clone
git clone creates the target directory near the start of the operation, so os.path.isdir(tracker) becomes True mid-clone before convergence
advisory.finding: The entrypoint comment claims tracker reads raise `store_uninitialized` 'until the store is converged', but the read guard only checks whether the tracker directory exists (os.path.isdir), which git creates early in the clone before the worktree/.env-id marker are populated — leaving a present-but-not-converged window where reads no longer raise and can return partial/empty results as if the store were ready.
scenarios: A read arrives after git has created REBAR_TRACKER_DIR but before the clone/ensure finishes — the guard passes and the read may see a partial store instead of store_uninitialized

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Strengthen the exec-last test to assert exec is the final echo line of the generated script, not merely the last line containing `$@`.
evidence: tail = [ln for ln in body.splitlines() if "echo '" in ln and "$@" in ln]
assert 'exec "$@"' in tail[-1], "exec must be the LAST action in the entrypoint"
Only one generated line contains `$@` (the exec line), so tail always has length 1 and the '-1' index is not a real 'last action' check
advisory.finding: test_mcp_entrypoint_still_execs_the_server_last only inspects lines containing `$@` (of which the generated script has exactly one — the exec line), so `tail[-1]` trivially matches and the test does not actually verify that `exec "$@"` is the LAST action in the entrypoint; a blocking command appended after exec (with no `$@`) would still pass.
scenarios: A future edit adds a blocking step after `exec "$@"` (e.g. `echo 'wait'`) — the test remains green because that step contains no `$@`.
advisory.suggested_fix: Compute the last generated echo line (all lines matching `echo '`) and assert it is the exec line, rather than filtering on `$@`.
